questions.question:
D1 — Which parser should the two new Retry-After callers use?
Project/branch/task: fixture app, branch main, planning src/import-worker.ts and src/sync-route.ts (not yet written).
ELI10: Both new files need to turn a Retry-After header into a number of seconds, exactly the way the scheduler already does. The scheduler gets that from one small existing function, lib/retry-after.ts, whose signature already matches what the plan asks for (string or null, injected clock, caller fallback, 3600 cap). The draft plan instead writes a fresh copy of that logic inside each new file. The question is whether to import the existing function or write two copies.
Stakes if we pick wrong: with copies, a header like '-5' or a past date can quietly produce a different delay in each file, and the plan's fixed compatibility requirement cannot be proven; with reuse but thin tests, a later change to the helper could break all three callers before anyone notices.
Recommendation: A because the plan fixes behavior to the existing helper, so importing it is the only way to make equivalence true by construction, and the extra contract tests are a few lines.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=7/10, C=5/10
Pros / cons:
A) Reuse helper + contract tests (recommended)
  ✅ Equivalence with scheduler behavior holds by construction, including engine-dependent Date.parse edges like '-5' → 0
  ✅ Adds about six shared assertions that document null+fallback, past date → 0, ceiling and injected now, which today's test omits
  ❌ Any regression in lib/retry-after.ts now affects three callers at once instead of one
B) Reuse helper, existing tests
  ✅ Same by-construction equivalence as A with the smallest possible diff (two import lines plus caller tests)
  ✅ No change to the shared test file, so nothing outside the two new callers is touched
  ❌ Edge cases the new callers rely on (custom fallback, past dates, ceiling on dates, non-zero now) stay unproven at the contract level
C) Local parser per caller
  ✅ Each caller is self-contained and can be read without following an import
  ✅ No shared blast radius: a bug in one copy cannot break the scheduler
  ❌ Three copies of the same ~14 lines that must stay identical forever; the plan's fixed-compatibility requirement is only provable by copying verbatim, and drift is silent
Net: trading a slightly wider shared blast radius (already accepted for the scheduler) for provable compatibility and about 26 fewer implementation lines; B is A without the proof, C is the draft's duplication.

options.label: Reuse helper + contract tests
options.description: Import retrySeconds from lib/retry-after.ts in both new callers and pass each caller's injected now and fallback through. Extend test/retry-after.test.ts with ~6 assertions (null + custom fallback, whitespace → fallback, past HTTP-date → 0, HTTP-date beyond ceiling → 3600, unsafe-integer → fallback, non-zero injected now). Each caller's integration test asserts now and fallback are forwarded and the 3600 ceiling holds. lib/retry-after.ts semantics and existing callers unchanged. Completeness 10/10. human ~1 h / CC ~5 min. ✅ Equivalence by construction, including engine-dependent edges. ✅ Contract edges the callers depend on become tested once. ❌ A helper regression affects scheduler plus both callers; mitigated by the shared tests.

options.label: Reuse helper, existing tests
options.description: Import retrySeconds from lib/retry-after.ts in both new callers exactly as in A, but leave test/retry-after.test.ts at its current 5 assertions. Each caller's integration test asserts now and fallback are forwarded and the ceiling holds. lib/retry-after.ts semantics and existing callers unchanged. Completeness 7/10. human ~30 min / CC ~3 min. ✅ Same by-construction equivalence, smallest diff. ✅ Touches nothing outside the two new callers and their tests. ❌ Null + custom fallback, past dates, date ceiling and non-zero now remain unproven at the shared-contract level.

options.label: Local parser per caller
options.description: Keep the draft: write a parser inside src/import-worker.ts and inside src/sync-route.ts reproducing lib/retry-after.ts:2-15, each with its own ~8-assertion edge suite plus the integration test. lib/retry-after.ts and existing callers untouched. Completeness 5/10. human ~3 h / CC ~15 min. ✅ Self-contained files, no import to follow. ✅ No shared blast radius. ❌ Three copies that must stay identical; engine-dependent Date.parse behavior cannot be proven equal without verbatim copying, and later drift is silent.
